title: The Tale of the First Brother, the Hunchbacked Tailor

paragraphs.en: The eldest brother, a tailor in Baghdad, fell in love with a lady he saw at his rich neighbor's bay window. He gazed at her all day until evening, then returned home dejectedly. The next morning, he resumed his vigil, only to faint when she appeared again.
paragraphs.zh: 大哥哥是巴格达的一名裁缝，他被邻居家阳台上一位女士吸引，整天注视着她直到傍晚。回到家时，心情沮丧。第二天一早，他又守在那儿，结果当那女士再次出现时，竟然晕了过去。

paragraphs.en: Recovering, he went home sullen.
paragraphs.zh: 恢复过来后，他闷闷不乐地回到了家中。

paragraphs.en: On the third day, the lady noticed him staring and smiled. She sent a maid with fine linen, asking him to make a blouse. He accepted her request and completed it quickly.
paragraphs.zh: 第三天，那位女士注意到他一直在盯着她看，便微微一笑。她派了一个婢女送来质地细腻的亚麻布，请他制作一件衬衫。他欣然答应，并很快完成了任务。

paragraphs.en: The following morning, the maid returned with another message: the lady was sleepless, thinking of him, and requested trousers to match the blouse. The tailor agreed and worked diligently on them.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天一早，女仆又带来了消息：那位小姐整晚辗转反侧，想着他，请求裁制一条与那件上衣相配的裤子。裁缝答应了，便专心致志地做起活来。

paragraphs.en: When the lady appeared again, she insisted he finish the trousers before leaving. Exhausted from his labors, the tailor borrowed money for food and returned home, unable to eat.
paragraphs.zh: 当那位女士再次出现时，她坚持要裁缝在离开前完成裤子的制作。经过一番劳作后精疲力尽，裁缝借了钱买些食物才得以回家，却连饭都吃不下。

paragraphs.en: The next morning, Shahrazad arrived at the shop when a maid informed her that the master wished to see her. She was relieved upon hearing this was good news, not punishment. The master asked her brother to make shirts from a large piece of Dabiqi linen.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天一早，沙赫拉兹德正要赶到裁缝店时，一个女仆告诉她主人想见她。听到这话，她松了一口气，心想这应该是好消息而不是惩罚。主人让她哥哥用一块大大的达比基亚亚亚亚亚亚亚亚麻布来做衬衫。

paragraphs.en: That night, Shahrazad continued her tale:
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，沙哈尔扎德继续讲述她的故事：

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad told the king that the tailor recounted how his brother made twenty shirts and trousers by evening without eating. When asked for payment, he requested twenty dirhams. The husband ordered scales brought to weigh the money.
paragraphs.zh: 沙赫拉扎德对国王说，裁缝讲述了他哥哥如何在晚餐前完成了二十件衬衫和裤子的制作，而且一整天都没有进食。当被要求付款时，哥哥要了二十迪尔汗作为报酬。丈夫吩咐拿来秤来称量这笔钱。

paragraphs.en: The wife approached, seemingly upset at the payment, but her brother insisted on taking nothing. Despite needing food, he left with his work, surviving only two loaves of bread for three days.
paragraphs.zh: 妻子似乎对这笔报酬不满，但哥哥坚持不要任何东西。尽管家里缺粮，他还是带着活计离开了，在接下来的三天里只靠两片面包勉强维持生计。

paragraphs.en: The maid approached my brother and asked, "What have you done?" He replied, "They are finished," and took them to his husband. The husband paid him but my brother refused the money out of fear for the lady.
paragraphs.zh: 女仆走近我哥哥，问道：“你做了什么？”他回答说：“都做好了。”然后把东西拿给他的丈夫。丈夫付了钱给他，但我的哥哥出于对那位女士的顾虑，拒绝收下这笔钱。

paragraphs.en: That night, he returned home hungry and restless.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，他回家时饥肠辘辘，心神不定。

paragraphs.en: The next morning, the maid summoned him again. My brother cut five robes and felt miserable as he went home empty-handed. He brought the robes to the husband, who praised his work.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天一早，女仆又把他叫了去。我的哥哥裁好了五件袍子，空手而归，心里满是沮丧。他把袍子交给丈夫，对方对他称赞了一番。

paragraphs.en: However, when the husband reached for a purse, my brother hesitated, remembering the lady's signal not to take it.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，当丈夫伸手去拿钱包时，我的弟弟犹豫了一下，想起那位女士曾暗示不要拿。

paragraphs.en: Later, the husband and wife tricked him into marrying their maid. When he tried to consummate the marriage, they sent him to sleep in the mill instead. In the middle of the night, the miller arrived, complaining that the wheel had stopped turning.
paragraphs.zh: 后来，这对夫妇设下计谋，让他娶了他们的女仆。当他试图完成婚事时，他们却让他去磨坊睡觉。午夜时分，磨坊主突然来到，抱怨说磨盘停转了。

paragraphs.en: He tied my brother to the yoke with a rope.
paragraphs.zh: 他用绳子把哥哥绑在了犁架上。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad paused her story, and Dinarzad remarked, "What an intriguing tale!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night; I have more to tell you if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 沙赫拉扎德暂停了故事，迪纳兹达remarked道：“真是引人入胜！”沙赫拉扎德回答说：“等到明天晚上再听吧；如果国王饶恕我，我会给你讲更多。”

paragraphs.en: The tailor recounted to King China a tale told by the barber to guests, who in turn heard it from a caliph. In the story, his hunchbacked brother was tied to a mill yoke and beaten by their father, the miller, as he ground wheat day and night. The brother could barely rest due to the constant beating.
paragraphs.zh: 裁缝向中国国王讲述了理发师对客人们讲述的一个故事，而这些客人又是从一位苏丹那里听来的。在这个故事中，他的驼背弟弟日日夜夜在磨坊里推着磨石磨面粉，父亲——那位磨坊主却把他绑在磨架上，不断地毒打他。弟弟几乎无法得到片刻的休息。

paragraphs.en: At dawn, the miller left him almost dead. A maid soon approached, offering sympathy for her mistress's sleepless worry over his condition. But the brother was too exhausted to respond.
paragraphs.zh: 黎明时分，磨坊主几乎让他奄奄一息。不久，一个女仆走过来，为她主人因他的状况而彻夜担忧表示同情。但这位兄弟已经疲惫不堪，无力回应。

paragraphs.en: He returned home, where a fortune-teller visited, claiming to see signs of love and happiness in his face. The brother retorted that he had merely worked all night at the mill instead. He then shared his ordeal with the fortune-teller, who said their stars did not align.
paragraphs.zh: 他回到家，正巧遇到一位算命先生来访。算命先生说从他的面相上看出了爱情和幸福的征兆。哥哥反驳道自己只是整晚在磨坊加班而已。接着，他向算命先生倾诉了自己的遭遇，算命先生则告诉他二人的命运并不相符。

paragraphs.en: The brother went back to his shop, hoping for work. A maid summoned him, but he refused her request. When she told his mistress, the lady appeared in the window, weeping and asking what was wrong.
paragraphs.zh: 哥哥回到他的店铺，希望能找到些活计。一个女仆叫住了他，但他婉拒了她的请求。女仆把这件事告诉了他的主人，女士随即出现在窗口，泪眼婆娑地问他出了什么问题。

paragraphs.en: The brother's heart softened at her beauty, and he forgave her.
paragraphs.zh: 哥哥被她的美貌打动，随即原谅了她。

paragraphs.en: A few days later, the maid informed Shahrazad that her husband would spend the night at a friend's house and asked Shahrazad to join them when he left. However, the truth was that the husband had given up on their tailor brother. The wife decided to play a trick on him in front of the entire city.
paragraphs.zh: 几天后，女仆告诉沙赫拉兹德，她的丈夫将去朋友家过夜，并请沙赫拉兹德在他离开时一同前往。然而，真相是丈夫已经放弃了他们那位驼背裁缝兄弟。妻子决定在全城人的面前给他一个下马威。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad did not share this story with Dinarzad until the next night. She said, "Brother, what an intriguing tale!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait and see; I have many more stories for you."
paragraphs.zh: 沙赫拉扎德直到第二天晚上才把这个故事告诉迪纳兹德。她说：“哥哥，这可真是个引人入胜的故事！”沙赫拉扎德回答道，“耐心点吧；我还有许多精彩的故事要给你听呢。”

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad began her narrative:
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，沙海拉罕开始了她的讲述：

paragraphs.en: O King, my brother approached the lady and asked for a quick kiss. Before he could finish speaking, his husband appeared from another room, declaring that he would not let him go until he was handed over to the chief of police. Despite pleading, the husband took my brother to the chief, who gave him one hundred lashes and paraded him through the city on a camel with a crier announcing his punishment for trespassing upon other people's wives.
paragraphs.zh: 国王啊，我哥哥走近那位女士，请求给她一个快速的吻。话音未落，他的丈夫从另一个房间出现，断然表示不会让他离开，除非将他交给警长。尽管我哥哥苦苦哀求，丈夫还是把他带到了警长那里。警长下令鞭打了他一百下，并且骑着骆驼在城中游行示众，还派了一个喊话的人宣布他的罪行是擅自闯入别人的妻子身边。

paragraphs.en: The prefect then banished him from the city, and he left without knowing where to go. But I followed him and cared for him.
paragraphs.zh: 知府随后将他驱逐出城，他茫然不知该往何处去。但我跟着他，并照顾着他。

paragraphs.en: When the caliph heard this story, he laughed and said, "Well done, O Silent One and man of few words!" He instructed me to take a gift and leave. However, I insisted on telling him about my other brothers' stories before accepting any gifts.
paragraphs.zh: 当哈里发听了这个故事后，他笑了笑，说道：“妙哉，沉默者、少言寡语之人！”他吩咐我先带礼物离开。但我坚持要在接受任何礼物之前，把其他兄弟的故事也告诉他。
